title: Micro Onboard Variant Playbook — scratch
content:
Context / goal:
- Problem: our developer onboarding is one-size-fits-all. big drop-off at first API call, confusion around keys/scopes, and poor early signal for cost and quotas.
- Aim: prototype lightweight, switchable micro-onboarding variants that adapt to user archetype and surface exactly the hooks they need to ship a first feature in <30 minutes.
- Outcome metrics (quick): time-to-first-successful-call, 7-day retention of API calls, percent who complete the quickstart tutorial, # of support tickets in first 14 days.

Hypotheses:
1) If we present 3 microflows (CLI-first, JS-SDK, No-code) tailored to detected intent, we increase time-to-first-successful-call < 15 min for power users and <30 min for product teams.
2) Small interactive examples (editable sample with live fake response) reduce confusion more than static docs.
3) Offering an opt-in sandbox key with tokens/limits improves trust and reduces early billing questions -> fewer support tickets.

Archetypes we care about (fast prioritization):
- Proto Hacker: wants a quick curl or Python snippet. Dev-first, low patience for UI.
- Product Integrator: working on a product feature, prefers JS/SDK, needs runbook and example schema.
- Data/ML Engineer: cares about embeddings/throughput, will want dedicated examples for batch embeddings and cost estimates.
- PM/Designer: wants a no-code playground + sample assistant templates.

Variant sketches (microflows):
A) CLI-First (Proto Hacker)
- Landing: detect "developer" intent via quick survey + past repo link if provided.
- Show: minimal curl + expected response, copyable, one-click run in ephemeral sandbox (no card required).
- Next step: GitHub gist generation with README template.
- Instrument: event: onramp_flow_started, snippet_copied, sandbox_run_result = success/failure.

B) JS-SDK Guided (Product Integrator)
- Landing: show small app scaffold (React) with placeholder UI and SDK wiring.
- Toggle: demo data vs. real key.
- Offer: code exports (codesandbox / StackBlitz) and a link to a preconfigured repo.
- Instrument: export_clicked, sandbox_connected, route-to-console (open dedicated onboarding panel).

C) No-code Playground (PM/Designer)
- Visual builder: create assistant from templates, drag-and-drop tool buttons (function calling stubbed).
- Shareable preview link.
- Prompt recipes for tuning tone and length.

D) Bulk Embedding Quickstart (Data/ML Eng)
- Small sample showing embedding batch pipeline (pandas -> embeddings -> vector DB).
- Inline cost estimate per 1k rows + recommended quantization/throughput settings.

Quick experiments matrix (MVPs):
- Experiment 1: One-click ephemeral sandbox for curl (A). Metric: successful_sandbox_runs / sandbox_invites > 0.6 within 24h. 2-week run.
- Experiment 2: JS scaffold export to codesandbox (B). Metric: repo_forks / exports. 2-week run.
- Experiment 3: No-code template share (C). Metric: share_clicks leading to visit by another user. 3-week run.
- Experiment 4: Embedding pipeline snippet with cost estimate (D). Metric: follow-up embedding requests within 7 days. 3-week run.

Instrumentation checklist (minimal):
- events: onramp_start, variant_assigned, step_completed, api_call_success, sandbox_run_result, export_generated, help_clicked, billing_concern_flagged
- attributes: user_archetype, initial_region, plan_tier, created_project_id
- dashboards: time-to-first-call distribution by archetype, funnel (started -> snippet copied -> run -> success), support tickets tagged "onboard" by cohort

Gatekeeping & privacy notes:
- Sandbox keys must be time-limited and read-only for certain routes (no long-lived secrets).
- For Private/Dedicated customers: default to a 'guided config' that helps map to their VPC endpoints rather than sandbox.

Rollout plan (fast):
- Week 0: internal alpha — product + DX + 2 partner customers. manual opt-in.
- Week 2: telemetry collection, iterate UX copy.
- Week 4: open beta to new signups behind an experiment flag (10% bucket).
- Week 8: analyze; promote to default for selected archetypes if metrics improve.

Open questions / TODOs:
- How to detect archetype without asking too many questions? quick heuristics: email domain + selected primary use case + repo link detection. test in alpha.
- What limits to expose in sandbox (rate, token size)? ask infra & SRE.
- Do we offer pre-seeded datasets for embeddings demo? cost/PRIV implications.
- Provide copy for support flow when sandbox fails -> quick troubleshooting checklist.

Engineering notes (implementation ideas):
- Lightweight variant system: meta config JSON per flow with steps, snippets, sample payloads. simple versioning so we can A/B a copy change.
- Small SDK helper: onboarding.startFlow({variant: 'cli-first', projectId}) -> returns ephemeralKey + sampleRequest + consoleLink.
- Prefer server-side generation of ephemeral keys with strict scopes + short TTL.

Prototype snippet (pseudo):
- JS: const {ephemeralKey, sample} = await onboard.startFlow({variant:'js-sdk'});
- Curl: curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $EPHEMERAL" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{...}'

Notes to self (voice):
- Keep the MVP narrow: focus on the first successful API call and a copyable artifact (codesandbox or gist).
- Make flow reversible (user can jump to full console).
- Keep legal/sales loop informed if we introduce sandbox keys for early customers.

Slack hooks / references:
- ping #dx-onboarding for UX help
- link to sketches: CONFLUENCE-ONRAMP-42

Next actions (this week):
- Draft minimal meta-config schema (Victor).
- Quick mock for CLI-First sandbox flow (Cleo).
- Ask infra for ephemeral key constraints & TTL (Zhen).
- Schedule 30-min alpha sync with 2 partners (add to calendar).

-- end scratch --

(Loose, incomplete; capture as a personal playbook for quick prototyping. Revisit with data after alpha.)
